objective: Establish Teams as an AppSDK 0.1.6-governed design project for a cross-agent DSH and OpenCode control console. The project records shared desktop/mobile UI semantics, nested drawer interaction, daemon-runtime/network composition, configuration-server admission, and host adapters without starting runtime implementation.

boundary.payload_control_separation: Bootstrap link configuration, endpoint, machine identity, generation, health, auth grant, permission decision, routing, reconnect, diagnostics, and runtime lifecycle are typed control resources. They must never enter business request/response payloads or metadata. Business payloads must never reconstruct control state.

acceptance_criteria: Teams is initialized as an AppSDK 0.1.6 project with governance contracts, maps, lifecycle manifest, and sdk.lock.

The design records one owner each for bootstrap link configuration, network transport and health, shared runtime configuration, account and permission admission, server listener and connection registry, daemon runtime lifecycle, agent/session semantics, capability publication, and UI projection.
Daemon runtime composes runtime lifecycle with network connection lifecycle; Agent remains network-agnostic and consumes an upper-layer runtime abstraction.

A control server can discover live daemon runtimes, share and synchronize configuration, authenticate accounts, and evaluate permissions without storing session messages, tool results, or approval bodies.

DSH and OpenCode compatibility is explicit: shared domain and typed federation semantics, separate DSH ClientContext/Slot and OpenCode PluginInput/Hooks adapters, and no claim of a shared host UI bundle.
The static HTML prototype is included as Playground design evidence with direct current-session navigation, reusable DSH Conversation surface, and nested drawer gestures.
No runtime implementation or source modification outside Teams is started before the governance maps and lifecycle manifest are admitted.
non_goals: Implement or publish a runtime plugin in this design-only change.
Modify DSH, OpenCode, their installed profiles, or the official DSH WebUI.
Store business session content in the control server.
Give master/slave relations implicit authority over agents or high-risk actions.
Treat DSH and OpenCode as if they share one UI mounting protocol.
Add fallback, silent payload stripping, or duplicate network/config/session implementations.
assumptions: The control server is a separately deployable server module and is reached through the configured network plugin transport.
Bootstrap link configuration is available before shared runtime configuration synchronization begins.
The server module owns deployment, listener, server-side connection registry, account admission, and permission decisions; the network plugin owns client link configuration, transport, and health.
The current DSH Conversation/Session rendering path remains the presentation owner for a focused DSH session.
Desktop and mobile share semantic components and action/state contracts; only layout and responsive composition differ.
The initial local Console Hub is the default deployment shape pending approval of the final product decision.

questions.question: Is this a new project, module refactor, project refactor, or debug task?
Which relative directory is the new AppSDK project root?
questions.answer: Teams/ at the repository root; its AppSDK project root is Teams/.

questions.question: Which existing directories remain read-only and outside the new project?
questions.answer: Existing DSH/OpenCode source, installed profiles, dsh-tui, and maui-0830 remain outside Teams; maui-0830 design files are read-only source evidence only.

questions.question: Which directories may the new project create or modify?
questions.answer: Only Teams/** for this design/governance milestone. Runtime code is not started.
